data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Myrrhine was a sea goddess. The name Myrian is the neuter form of this name, which may suggest a connection to the sea or maritime themes. In the Bible, myrrh is a fragrant resin that was used as a gift to the infant Jesus and as an embalming substance. The name Myrian carries the meaning “Neuter form of Myrrhine (sea goddess)” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Myrian usually hope their child will grow to embody neuter form of myrrhine (sea goddess) and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Myrian, as the neuter form of the Greek goddess name Myrrhine, could potentially evoke maritime associations. This is reminiscent of the biblical Magi, who arrived by ship to present gifts to the newborn Jesus. Myrrh was one of these gifts, contributing to the nautical theme.
data.spiritual_significance: Myrrh is described in the Bible as a precious and fragrant substance that was used to anoint the body of Jesus. In Christian tradition, myrrh symbolizes sorrow, suffering, and the sweetness of sacrifice. Since Myrian is the neuter form of Myrrhine, it may be seen as a reminder of the sacrifice Jesus made for humanity and the preciousness of the Christian faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Myrian: A beacon of grace and faith, illuminating the way for seekers on their spiritual journey. Inspired by the countless stars in the night sky, a Myrian shines brightly with God's love.
